master.master_headline: Holding at 8 on summit day: Gulf pressure is better confirmed, but nothing has broken yet.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. Same method as before: anchor on the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. All sixteen desks held their own figures this edition. The one change I make is small: the fact-checker now confirms the Hormuz shortfall (about 65% below pre-war in a named weekly shipping report) and Egypt's deeper gas cut to fertiliser plants, so the food and resources clock comes in a little. Against that, Ebola growth is steady, food prices are still mild, no credit stress has appeared, and the Shenzhen leaders' meeting and the IAEA board outcome were both unreported when the desks filed. One small resources move does not shift a board this wide, so the master holds at 8 with a steady trend; steady means no net movement, not that the risks eased.

most_pressing.title: Xi, Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen on 19 Nov
most_pressing.why: The first three-way leaders' meeting comes with no US-Russia arms treaty in force and Gulf attacks continuing; the US agenda is arms cuts and Iran, not Ukraine, and China wants the US and Russia to cut first.

most_pressing.title: Hormuz traffic about 65% below pre-war as Egypt deepens fertiliser gas cuts
most_pressing.why: Shipping and fertiliser supply are squeezed at the same time as a likely historic El Nino heads into 2027 harvests.

most_pressing.title: Iran says no enriched uranium will leave the country
most_pressing.why: About 440 kg of highly enriched uranium remains unseen by inspectors while the IAEA board meets, with Iran rejecting normal inspections.

most_pressing.title: AI-led stock slide as a half-point December Fed hike is debated
most_pressing.why: Rate pressure and concentrated AI valuations meet on 8-9 December, though growth and jobs are still firm.

most_pressing.title: Ebola passes 11,000 cases with most new cases untraced
most_pressing.why: There is no licensed vaccine for this strain and over 80% of new cases are off contact lists, though weekly growth is steady.

master.where_headed: The next days hinge on the Shenzhen leaders' meeting (19 Nov), the IAEA board's close and the COP31 close around 20 Nov, and Kilauea's episode window to 22 Nov. After that: Israel's coalition deadline on 6 Dec (extendable), FAA and SpaceX follow-ups, the Fed meeting on 8-9 Dec with a hike expected and its size debated, US inflation data on 10 Dec, and France's push for an EU sanctions list within about a month. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI capability and investment running ahead of oversight, and a strong El Nino meeting 2027 harvests while Gulf shipping and fertiliser stay tight. Mitigants keep advancing but arrive too late for this window.
cross_links: Iran war to Hormuz to food: confirmed shipping data shows Gulf transits about 65% below pre-war, and with Egypt's fertiliser gas cut deepening, the war now presses on 2027 harvest inputs as well as energy prices.
Iran war to nuclear and cyber: the same conflict keeps uranium unverified and sits behind the refrigeration attacks France attributes to Iran's Revolutionary Guards.
El Nino to food and climate: NOAA gives about 60% odds of a historic event, already tied to famine risk in Sudan, while COP31 struggles over finance and fossil wording.
AI boom to economy and chips: the record AI listing, chipmakers buying into it, and an AI-led stock slide tie market risk to one race while rates rise.
Summit to several desks: the Shenzhen meeting could ease or harden arms control, Iran and trade at once, so it remains the single event most likely to move several clocks together next edition.
master.dissent: A reader could argue for 7.5: the Hormuz shortfall is now confirmed, Egypt's cut deepened, ship attacks hit a monthly record in October, Ebola is mostly untraced, and the stock slide shows the AI-and-rates pressure point is live. The case for 8.5 is also there: no desk moved on its own evidence, food prices are mild, Ebola growth is flat, banks are sound, and any Iran de-escalation from Shenzhen would ease several desks at once.
changes_since_last: Food and resources moved slightly closer: a named weekly shipping report puts Hormuz traffic about 65% below pre-war, and Egypt raised its gas cut to fertiliser plants from 20% to 33%.
Gulf fighting continued rather than escalated: drones fired at a US radar in Bahrain were intercepted, and Qatar convened new talks with Iran.
US stocks fell on 17 Nov, led by AI shares, while the half-point December Fed hike debate continued.
The record AI listing priced above its range, and Nvidia's leadership change is now confirmed by several outlets; neither moved a clock.
Eased or flat: Ebola weekly growth stayed near 500 with no new exports, solar storms stayed minor at mid-latitudes, and no new cyber escalation appeared.
Still pending: the Shenzhen leaders' meeting, the IAEA board outcome and the COP31 close were all unreported when the desks filed.
master.edition_note: A twelve-hour follow-up in which every desk held and the clock-setter made one small confirmed move (resources), with the main swing events still pending, so put very little weight on this edition's movement.

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: Anthropic prices record IPO at $83, above range; AI-R&D threshold flagged
desks.summary: Anthropic priced its IPO on 18 Nov at $83 per share, above the $70-78 range, at about a $1.5 trillion valuation, with Nasdaq trading as ANT expected 19 Nov. Its S-1 amendment says models may soon reach its threshold for rapid AI-driven R&D, and METR estimates about twice the earlier pace. Frontier cyber models are being released only to vetted users while regulators delay rather than tighten rules.

desks.name: Biosecurity & Pandemics
desks.midnight_definition: A pandemic or biological event worse than COVID-19 in global deaths and disruption.
desks.headline: Ebola >11,200 cases, Africa CDC: 80% of new cases untraced; pandemic annex slips to 2027
desks.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC is the second-largest on record: UKHSA reports 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of 9 Nov (510 more cases in a week), and a Reuters report of 17 Nov cites over 11,200 infections and 5,500 deaths. Africa CDC says over 80% of new cases come from outside contact lists. Exports remain contained (Kenya 9 cases, none since 19 Oct; Nigeria 1 case; Uganda over). The pathogen-sharing annex of the pandemic agreement missed the May 2026 target and is now due no later than May 2027.

top_stories.title: Ebola in DR Congo passes 11,000 confirmed cases; response hit by attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Official institute figures show 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths across eight provinces; youths burned an Ebola treatment facility in Ituri and militia clashes paused work in one area. Ervebo is entering a trial to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

top_stories.title: Africa CDC: Ebola over 11,200 cases, most new cases untraced, funds unreleased
top_stories.why_it_matters: Africa CDC says over 80% of new cases are outside contact lists and over 65% of deaths occur in the community; about $2.9bn pledged but donors are urged to release about $1.6bn; some health workers unpaid for months.

top_stories.title: UKHSA week 45: DRC 11,042 cases, North Kivu now ahead of Ituri
top_stories.why_it_matters: Cases rose by 510 and deaths by 261 in the week to 9 Nov, across 67 health zones in 8 provinces; North Kivu now adds about 31 cases a day against 29 in Ituri. WHO risk is very high in DRC, high for neighbours, low globally.

top_stories.title: US has lost measles elimination status, health authorities say
top_stories.why_it_matters: A US administration official confirmed the revocation after 26 years; experts say regaining it requires more vaccination and better surveillance. A PAHO page confirming this was not seen.

top_stories.title: Washington State reports first US bird flu death of 2026
top_stories.why_it_matters: Fatal H5N1 case in Yakima County with dairy cattle exposure; officials rate public risk as low and no person-to-person spread was reported.

top_stories.title: Pandemic agreement pathogen-sharing annex pushed to no later than May 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: Member states failed to finish the annex by the May 2026 Assembly and agreed to continue; the treaty cannot open for signature until it is adopted. Outcome of the 2-13 Nov ninth round still not found.

trajectory.six_months: Ebola likely stays at roughly 450 to 550 confirmed cases a week in DRC given insecurity and untraced cases; US measles likely rises into spring; H5N1 human cases stay sporadic; annex talks continue toward the May 2027 Assembly.
trajectory.two_years: Outcome hinges on whether the PABS annex is agreed and surveillance and vaccination capacity recover. A COVID-scale event remains a tail risk rather than a baseline.

desks.bottom_line: Treat the DRC Ebola outbreak as a prolonged, uncontrolled regional emergency with low but real export risk; funding release, paying and protecting responders and contact tracing are the levers.
desks.why_it_matters: Millions in eastern DRC and neighbours face an outbreak with no licensed vaccine, while treaty gaps and weakened health systems limit the world's readiness for the next one.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: Yale review: epigenetic-age drops seen, but no proof they mean longer healthy life
desks.summary: A Nature Medicine analysis of 51 human intervention studies found lifestyle changes, metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF drugs lowered epigenetic age markers, but the authors say it is unknown whether this translates into longer or healthier lives. Merck and Moderna's personalised melanoma vaccine hit both Phase 3 endpoints (announced 19 Aug 2026) and the companies say they will engage regulators on filing; no filing is confirmed. Narrow-disease progress continues, with nothing yet on a broad human ageing endpoint.

top_stories.title: Yale-led review of 51 trials: which interventions shift epigenetic age
top_stories.why_it_matters: Largest human check of ageing-clock responsiveness: exercise plus diet, metformin, semaglutide and anti-TNF drugs moved the markers, supplements did not. The outcome was a biomarker, not lifespan or disease, so it does not meet the midnight threshold.

top_stories.title: Merck and Moderna announce melanoma vaccine met both Phase 3 endpoints
top_stories.why_it_matters: Press release says intismeran plus Keytruda improved recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival in resected stage IIB-IV melanoma; no hazard ratios published, data to be presented at a future meeting, and the companies will engage regulators on filing. Resolves last edition's date discrepancy in favour of 19 Aug, per trade press dated that day.

top_stories.title: OncLive: intismeran plus pembrolizumab meets RFS and DMFS endpoints
top_stories.why_it_matters: Independent trade-press report dated 19 Aug 2026 corroborating the announcement date (headline-level only, page not fetched).

top_stories.title: Moderna CEO: Merck partnership racing to file melanoma vaccine, approval expected 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: Stated filing intent and 2027 approval aim; a personalised cancer vaccine would be a single-disease first.

top_stories.title: Gene therapy approvals broaden: Casgevy label extended to age 2 and up
top_stories.why_it_matters: FDA widened Casgevy to children from age 2 (July 2026) and gave accelerated approval to a leukocyte adhesion deficiency gene therapy (March 2026). Gene medicine is widening, but only for rare disease.

trajectory.six_months: FDA decision on Intellia's lonvo-z due 10 March 2027; a melanoma vaccine filing announcement and full INTerpath-001 data are plausible; more rare-disease gene therapy actions. No broad anti-ageing therapy expected.
trajectory.two_years: Personalised vaccines and in vivo editing plausibly approved; ageing trials will probably still report biomarkers or single-disease endpoints until a validated clinical ageing endpoint is accepted.

signals_to_watch: FDA action on Intellia lonvo-z (target date 2027-03-10)
Merck/Moderna confirmation of an intismeran FDA submission and full INTerpath-001 data presentation
Any randomised ageing-intervention trial with a clinical endpoint (multi-disease incidence, function, mortality)
Verified Neuralink participant count and new UK/UAE trial starts
desks.clock_reasoning: Midnight needs a human-proven, broad anti-ageing therapy. The new Nature Medicine analysis shows some interventions move epigenetic clocks but explicitly leaves clinical meaning unknown, so it does not justify moving the clock. Holding at 24; a bullish reader could count GLP-1s and metformin as stepping stones and go lower, a sceptic can cite the missing validated ageing endpoint and go higher.

Neuralink participant count: one Nov 2026 newsletter says 12, while other results cite 21 enrolled (Jan 2026) and a 26th patient; conflicting, so no figure used
Synchron, Isomorphic, Verve status not researched this run
Yale study publication date: ScienceDaily posted 13 Nov, Yale link suggests release around 21 Aug
Base editing first BLA item (Insights.bio) remains title-level only and was not re-checked
desks.bottom_line: Expect narrow-disease gene and vaccine approvals through 2027, but do not plan around a proven broad anti-ageing therapy on this horizon.
desks.why_it_matters: Patients with rare genetic disease and resected melanoma benefit first; the ageing threshold, which would affect everyone, remains unproven, and biomarker headlines risk overstating progress.
desks.confidence_basis: Low: the ageing study was read via a secondary summary, several items are press releases or trade press without effect sizes, and BCI figures conflict.
would_change: A randomised human trial showing a drug cuts multi-disease incidence or mortality in older adults (closer)
Regulatory acceptance of an epigenetic or other biomarker as a surrogate ageing endpoint (closer)
Failure or safety halt of a leading in vivo editing programme, or FDA rejection of lonvo-z (farther)

affects.why: AI-designed drugs and models drive discovery pipelines in this field.
Costly one-time therapies and ageing claims raise access and ageing-population questions.

desks.since_last: Added the Nature Medicine epigenetic-clock review (biomarker only) and resolved the melanoma announcement date to 19 Aug 2026 via Merck and trade press. No human clinical ageing endpoint appeared, so the clock holds at 24.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. The epigenetic-clock review is a biomarker result with clinical meaning explicitly unknown; no broad human ageing therapy.

desks.name: Semiconductors & Quantum
desks.midnight_definition: A fault-tolerant quantum computer performs commercially or cryptographically relevant work (e.g. breaking RSA/elliptic-curve keys) that classical machines cannot.
desks.headline: Nvidia posts record quarter under interim CEO as US widens AI chip export net
desks.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned on 12 Nov amid a board investigation tied to Singapore firm Megaspeed; the US has opened a criminal probe of Megaspeed and issued a rule requiring licences for advanced AI chips to five countries. Despite this, Nvidia reported a record quarter on 17 Nov and guided higher. Quantum vendors keep reporting incremental error-correction progress and rising revenue, but no independent proof of fault tolerance exists.

top_stories.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns; CFO Kress interim CEO, Jones named chair
top_stories.why_it_matters: Leadership change at the dominant AI-chip supplier, linked to an investigation involving Megaspeed, raises succession and export-compliance risk for the AI compute supply chain.

top_stories.title: US moves to block remote access to AI chips; Megaspeed criminal probe confirmed
top_stories.why_it_matters: Licences are now needed to ship advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil; Commerce and Justice confirmed a criminal investigation into Megaspeed. Beijing denies the espionage allegations.

top_stories.title: Nvidia Q3 FY27: revenue $115.8B, Q4 guide $130B, zero China data-centre assumed
top_stories.why_it_matters: Demand for AI chips remains extremely strong even as policy and governance risk rise; the guide reportedly assumes no China data-centre compute sales. Live-blog figures, to be checked against Nvidia's release.

top_stories.why_it_matters: IonQ guided to $505-515M revenue for 2026 and Quantinuum Q3 revenue rose 233%; commercial momentum is real, though revenue is small and the digest mixes company claims.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Memory remains a bottleneck for AI hardware; gains are decelerating but positive.

The Nvidia and export news is a chips-supply story and does not move the quantum threshold. Holding at 10.0; an optimist would say under 8, a skeptic 15 or more.

desks.bottom_line: Expect AI chip supply to stay governed by export policy and Nvidia's leadership transition, and treat quantum 2029 dates as vendor goals until independently tested.
desks.why_it_matters: Nvidia supplies most AI accelerators, so governance and licence changes touch AI developers, cloud providers and allies in SE Asia. Quantum progress matters to anyone holding long-lived encrypted data.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 final day nears with EU warning on draft; NOAA: 60% odds of historic El Nino
desks.summary: COP31 in Antalya (scheduled to close 20 Nov) is working from an 18-page cover decision that includes fossil-fuel phase-out wording, a 1.5C overshoot reference and a 35% electrification goal; the EU envoy warned it could make talks untenable, the Arab Group and Russia oppose energy-specific targets, and Australia's Bowen signalled another draft. NOAA's 12 Nov update puts Nino 3.4 at +2.5C with about 60% odds of a historic event. No new tipping-element science was verified.

top_stories.title: EU warns COP31 draft could make talks untenable; another draft expected
top_stories.why_it_matters: Consensus rules let one party block; the draft asks for fossil phase-out and net zero for rich countries by 2030, and an IPCC AR7 timing dispute is also live. Overrun past 20 Nov is plausible.

top_stories.title: COP31 day-by-day: red lines on methane, electrification, adaptation finance
top_stories.why_it_matters: LMDCs object to methane being singled out; Arab Group and Russia oppose the 35% electrification goal; tripling adaptation finance (about 120bn USD figure) is pushed into finance talks by the EU, Japan and others.

top_stories.title: Draft carries two fossil wordings; Bowen says final will differ
top_stories.why_it_matters: One option repeats 2023 'transitioning away' wording and a stronger one says 'phase out'; either may be dropped.

top_stories.title: NOAA: El Nino strengthening, about 60% chance of historic strength
top_stories.why_it_matters: Over 79% odds of strong-to-very-strong through Jan-Mar 2027 raises odds of record 2027 heat, coral and weather stress.

top_stories.title: Pledged public climate finance from big donors about 70% below 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Aid cuts shrink adaptation money as disputes over developed-country obligations deepen.

top_stories.title: October 2026 warmest on record; 2026 virtually certain to top 1.5C
top_stories.why_it_matters: Record-strength El Nino building makes 2027 records likely.

trajectory.six_months: COP31 probably closes with a compromise cover decision, possibly after overrunning; El Nino peaks around the turn of the year and monthly temperature records are likely into early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: 2027 has a strong chance of record warmth and overshoot becomes the working assumption; clean-energy growth may flatten emissions but not relieve stress on coral, ice and ocean-circulation tipping elements.

signals_to_watch: Next COP31 draft and final cover decision (20 Nov, overrun possible): does fossil phase-out or transition wording survive?
Fate of 35% electrification goal, 1.5C overshoot language and adaptation finance tripling
IPCC AR7 timing dispute; IPCC session in December
NOAA ENSO update 10 Dec; Copernicus bulletin early Dec
desks.clock_reasoning: No new evidence on tipping-element timing, and COP31 remains unresolved, so the clock holds. The near-record El Nino adds near-term heat risk but is a cyclical driver, not a tipping event. This is judgment, not measurement; someone weighting tipping-point science as more imminent could place it under 5.
unverified: COP31 outcome and anything after 17 Nov (nothing newer indexed)
NOAA figures come via a local-news summary, not the CPC page itself
2026 AMOC, ice sheet, Amazon, permafrost findings: only substack or old items found
Extreme weather of the last 90 days
desks.bottom_line: Treat 1.5C overshoot and a record-warm 2027 as the planning baseline; watch the 20 Nov COP31 text for whether any fossil-exit language survives.
desks.why_it_matters: Weak or diluted outcomes and falling climate finance leave vulnerable and low-income countries more exposed to a record El Nino year and continued warming.
desks.confidence_basis: Medium: ENB, Al Jazeera and Al-Monitor agree on negotiating state to 17 Nov, but later days, NOAA's primary page and tipping science were not retrieved.
would_change: Closer: new peer-reviewed evidence of AMOC or ice-sheet destabilisation, or COP31 collapse without a text
Farther: COP31 deal with binding fossil-exit language and funded adaptation

Adaptation finance figure circulating in corridors

Next NOAA ENSO diagnostic discussion
Approximate: next Copernicus monthly bulletin (unconfirmed)

affects.why: Record heat and El Nino disrupt agriculture, insurance and energy demand.
Finance and fossil-fuel splits strain North-South and producer-consumer relations.
The 35% electrification goal and fossil language shape energy transition policy.

desks.name: Cyber & Critical Infrastructure
desks.midnight_definition: A cyberattack or cascading failure takes down critical infrastructure across a major country for weeks.
desks.headline: France blames Iran for fridge and PLC attacks; EU sanctions push pending, no new escalation
desks.summary: No new major incident surfaced since the 18 Nov edition. France's push (16 Nov) for an EU sanctions list over the October fridge campaign (about 700 sites, at least 15 fires), which France attributes to Iran's Revolutionary Guards, is pending. A US joint advisory on 5 Nov, which names no actor, and an EU-level warning on 4 Nov confirm a cross-border threat, with three French blood banks hit on 2-3 Nov and new waves in Sweden, Belgium and Luxembourg. US officials suspect, but have not confirmed, Iran-linked freezer disruption at about six military commissaries since late August. All effects remain local and recover in days.

top_stories.title: France to seek EU sanctions on Iran over fridge cyberattacks; 15 fires
top_stories.why_it_matters: A cyber campaign with physical effects is becoming a formal EU sanctions matter. Iran's UN mission did not respond in the coverage seen; Tehran routinely denies such operations.

top_stories.title: FBI, CISA and three agencies warn of attacks on refrigeration controllers
top_stories.why_it_matters: The US government says attackers are exploiting internet-exposed temperature controllers worldwide to force heating or defrost cycles. Sectors at risk include grocery, healthcare, chemicals and transport; the advisory names no actor.

top_stories.title: US warns on refrigeration hacks amid suspected military commissary attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Joint US agencies urge taking controllers offline; officials suspect Iran-linked disruption at about six military commissaries since late August. The US notice names no actor; the Iran comparison is an outside expert's view.

top_stories.title: CISA and partners extend Iran PLC advisory to Schneider and Siemens devices
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iranian-affiliated actors first hit Rockwell PLCs in April; the update widens targeting to other vendors. Corrects last edition's approximate November date.

top_stories.title: Cold-chain attack timeline: 13-country second wave, UK meat suppliers, Pentagon probe
top_stories.why_it_matters: An analyst timeline lists a 2 Nov second wave across 13 countries and a suspected cyber cause for August US commissary freezer failures. Counts differ from the US advisory (115 stores, six countries); some claims are unproven.

top_stories.title: FBI: Salt Typhoon still ongoing, reaching beyond telecoms, 80+ countries
top_stories.why_it_matters: An FBI official says the Chinese espionage campaign continues and has affected over 80 countries (his estimate). It is espionage, not disruption, but implies prepositioned access in telecoms.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an EU sanctions listing on Iranian IRGC-linked persons, more exploitation of exposed cold-chain and PLC devices, and copycat or retaliatory activity. Most incidents stay local and last days.
trajectory.two_years: A large pool of poorly secured operational technology, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and normalised state retaliation raise the odds of a multi-sector event, though hardening mandates (US advisories, UK bill) could blunt it.

signals_to_watch: EU foreign ministers' handling of France's evidence and any sanctions list (France said within about a month)
Formal US or UK attribution of the water, commissary or UK power incidents
Any attack on a large utility or grid operator rather than small operators
UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill: remaining Lords third reading and Commons consideration of amendments
Further FBI/CISA advisories on OT devices
desks.clock_reasoning: Held at 6.8: a state-linked campaign with fires and blood-bank exposure is serious, but every observed effect is local and recovered in days; no new evidence since the last edition. A resilience-minded reader could argue for 8; an AI-offence-focused one for 5.
unverified: Store counts conflict: France says about 700 sites (Ynet citing French agencies); the US advisory coverage says 250 to 350 French stores plus 115 in six countries; SOCRadar says 13 countries
Attribution of Minnesota water, UK power and non-French cold-chain attacks not confirmed by governments
GPS jamming, satellite and finance outage incidents, and Salt Typhoon developments after February, not found
Primary CISA pages not fetched; advisory read via secondary press
Commissary freezer cause remains suspected, not confirmed (Nextgov citing Reuters)
No new incidents found for 18-19 Nov; searches for finance, GPS and satellite incidents returned nothing usable
desks.bottom_line: Operators of refrigeration and water controllers should pull them off the public internet now; France wants an EU sanctions list within a month.
desks.why_it_matters: Food retailers, cold storage, hospitals and blood services, and small water utilities face physical consequences from weakly secured controllers, and a state-attribution fight raises escalation risk with Iran.
desks.confidence_basis: Official statements relayed by press and a US joint advisory agree on the campaign, but counts differ and I reached no primary government pages.
would_change: Closer: a successful attack on a grid operator or large water utility causing multi-day regional outage
Closer: new US/EU findings of destructive access across many sectors
Farther: broad remediation of exposed controllers and de-escalation with Iran

decision_points.what: Approximate end of the one-month window France gave for an EU sanctions list
Soft marker: EU foreign ministers' consideration of French evidence (date not confirmed)

affects.why: Attribution to the IRGC and EU sanctions feed Iran war escalation and Europe-Iran relations.
Iran-linked PLC attacks hit energy and water operators.
Food spoilage, fires and blood storage exposure hit the public directly.

desks.since_last: No new escalation found in the 12 hours since the last edition; clock holds at 6.8. Corrected the PLC advisory update date to 22 Jul and added the EU joint warning of 4 Nov and the military commissary suspicion.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. No new escalation in the twelve hours since last edition. The fact-checker notes the Iran link is France's attribution and a US suspicion; the US advisory names no actor.

notes: Ynet confirms France sanctions push 16 Nov, about 700 sites, at least 15 fires, Iran UN mission no response; France names the IRGC and wants a list within a month. BleepingComputer confirms FBI/CISA/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory 5 Nov, 115+ stores in six European countries, no actor named. Nextgov confirms about six commissaries since late August, Iran-linked is US officials' suspicion, no actor in the joint warning.

Headline says Iran-linked without attribution: it is France's attribution (IRGC) and unconfirmed US suspicion; US advisory names no actor. Bottom line 'expect EU-Iran sanctions escalation within weeks' is a forecast, softened below. Not checked: SOCRadar, AHA, CyberScoop, Scripps (KF 3).

desks.name: Global Economy & SPY
desks.midnight_definition: THREAT lens: a systemic financial crisis on the scale of 2008 or worse (disorderly bond/credit/bank failure with a deep equity collapse and a frozen financial system).
desks.headline: Dow drops 1.6% on 17 Nov as AI stocks slide; 50bp December Fed hike debated
desks.summary: US stocks fell on 17 Nov (S&P 500 7,340.53, -1.0%; Dow -1.6%; Nasdaq -0.7%), the first wire-grade index reading this run. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on 28 Oct with Governor Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissenting for a hike; minutes of that meeting were released on 18 Nov (content not checked). A hot October CPI revived talk of a 50bp December move. Growth and jobs remain firm, and no bank or credit failure was found.

top_stories.title: Wall Street slides: S&P 500 -1%, Dow -1.6% on 17 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: Gives a firm index level after conflicting aggregator figures: S&P 500 closed at 7,340.53, Dow 50,759.42, Nasdaq 24,328.38, a sizeable one-day drop amid hike worries.

top_stories.title: Primer: FOMC minutes of 28 Oct meeting due 18 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: Fed held at 3.75-4.00% with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a 25bp hike; minutes may look stale because they predate the hot CPI that revived 50bp talk.

top_stories.title: Fed's Waller says a 50bp December hike should be considered after hot CPI
top_stories.why_it_matters: A voting governor openly backing a larger move raised the odds of a jumbo hike; the 10-year rose 14bp to 5.00% and the 2-year 19bp to 4.738% that day. CME pricing that day still favoured 25bp (90.5%) over 50bp (9.5%).

top_stories.title: October CPI +0.4% m/m, above the 0.3% expected
top_stories.why_it_matters: A third straight upside surprise in prices; shelter rose 0.3% and energy 0.7%. No annual October rate was published because of the earlier shutdown data gap; September's annual rate was 3.7%.

top_stories.title: Bond yields top 5.13% while equities lag in pricing further hikes
top_stories.why_it_matters: Futures priced three quarter-point hikes through March (to 4.50-4.75%), while strategists warn stocks are not positioned for a longer cycle. A Fed governor flagged AI-related debt above $800B this year.

top_stories.title: Weekly review: 2-year yield surge, 50bp hike priced, Fed speakers, minutes due
top_stories.why_it_matters: Describes a roughly 35bp weekly rise in the 2-year yield, rate futures pricing a possible half-point December hike, GDP up 3.4% in Q3, oil down about 20% in a month, and public friction between the Treasury Secretary and the Fed over hiking.

trajectory.six_months: Base case is one to three more Fed hikes, long yields in a 4.5-5.5% range and choppy tech-led equities; lower oil could ease inflation, while a further hot print or AI-credit event would deepen stress.
trajectory.two_years: Record interest costs, AI capex debt, leveraged nonbank finance and bank bond losses could end in a soft landing with rotation away from AI leaders, or a disorderly deleveraging; analysts disagree widely.

signals_to_watch: Minutes of the last FOMC meeting (due week of Nov 16) and the Dec 8-9 decision: 25bp vs 50bp
November CPI on Dec 10, day after the Fed decision
10-year yield sustained above 5.3% (Oct 5 closing high 5.31%) or weak Treasury auctions
S&P 500 drawdown past 10% from its record, VIX above 30, or any AI-linked credit default
Oil path and Iran war developments

Held at 7.8: new evidence cuts both ways, with hike size debate and a 2-year surge pushing closer, but strong GDP, 4.1% unemployment, oil down 20% and well-capitalised banks pushing farther. Judgment, not measurement; a more worried reader would weight bond-equity divergence, a calmer one the strong growth data.

Current market-implied odds of a 50bp hike

desks.bottom_line: Expect a Dec 8-9 Fed hike of at least 25bp with real odds of 50bp; long yields above 5% are the pressure point to watch.

Farther: soft CPI on Dec 10, yields falling below 4.8%, continued oil decline

November CPI release

desks.name: Energy & Fusion
desks.midnight_definition: The first fusion plant delivers net electricity to a grid commercially, so energy abundance becomes a build-out problem rather than a physics problem.
desks.headline: Fusion cash above $13B but no net-electricity device; PJM grid gap persists
desks.summary: On data from June to August 2026: private fusion funding has passed $13B across 17 startups with over $100M each (TNW, 19 Jun), but no private company has shown net energy gain at commercial scale. SPARC was described as about 75% built and expected to reach burning plasma in late 2026 or early 2027; Helion targets 2028 electricity for Microsoft. On the grid side PJM faces a projected 50-60 GW decade deficit and proposed a one-time 6 GW backstop auction (planned for 30 Sep-21 Oct; outcome not checked).

top_stories.title: 17 fusion startups have each raised over $100M; total above $13B
top_stories.why_it_matters: Funding is at record scale and concentrated: Helion raised $465M at a $15.5B valuation in June. The piece stresses that no private firm has shown commercial-scale net energy.

top_stories.title: SPARC reported about 75% complete; burning plasma late 2026 or early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: The nearest-term fusion physics milestone. The same article puts CFS's ARC power plant in the early 2030s at the earliest, which anchors the clock.

top_stories.title: PJM members back hyperscaler plan; 50-60 GW decade deficit projected
top_stories.why_it_matters: Data-centre demand has produced PJM's first procurement shortfall and sharply higher capacity prices across 13 states, with political pressure on bills.

top_stories.title: PJM proposes one-time 6 GW reliability backstop auction
top_stories.why_it_matters: The plan, filed with FERC on 31 Jul and 7 Aug, is meant to restore break-even reliability. The page is undated, so the month is inferred from those filing dates.

top_stories.title: PJM says developers propose 800+ new power projects
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows supply is being proposed but the queue has not yet closed the gap in the largest US grid.

trajectory.six_months: Expect more fundraising, SPARC commissioning news and PJM/FERC backstop outcomes; no net-electricity fusion result is likely. Grid strain and power-price politics keep growing.
trajectory.two_years: SPARC may have first plasma and early results, and Helion will show whether 2028 holds. Grid-connected fusion electricity is still unlikely by end-2028; the 2030s remain the central estimate.

signals_to_watch: SPARC first plasma / burning plasma date and any further slip
Helion's 2028 Microsoft delivery date
FERC ruling on PJM's backstop procurement filings and auction result
Fusion Industry Association annual funding report (mid-2027)
Next PJM capacity auction results
desks.clock_reasoning: No plant has shown net electricity and credible plans cluster in the 2030s; Helion's 2028 date is viewed sceptically and SPARC dates have slipped before. Nothing seen this run justifies a move. This is informed judgment: faith in Helion would put it under 10, weighting slippage above 20.
unverified: SPARC magnet count and exact schedule after June 2026 not confirmed; a webpronews page and CFS site could not be fetched
Energy-storage.news backstop auction page is undated; the 30 Sep-21 Oct window and FERC status were not confirmed as current
Outcome of the autumn PJM backstop auction not found
Helion Orion, ITER, NIF and storage/solar statistics not covered; no last-48-hour news found
desks.bottom_line: Plan for grid scarcity this decade and treat fusion electricity as a 2030s event; SPARC and Helion milestones are the dates to track.
desks.why_it_matters: Data-centre demand is straining the largest US grid and raising prices now, while fusion relief lies beyond this decade; utilities, households and AI builders are affected.
desks.confidence_basis: Medium: rests on dated press reports (TNW, E&E News) agreeing that no net-electricity device exists, but several figures are months old and some pages were undated or unreachable.
would_change: A SPARC burning-plasma or net-gain result earlier than 2027 would move the clock closer
Helion delivering grid power to Microsoft by 2028 would move it sharply closer
A further SPARC or Helion slip, or a funding failure, would move it farther

Approx. Fusion Industry Association annual funding report (date unconfirmed)
End of CFS's 2027 window for SPARC first plasma / burning plasma

affects.why: Data-centre load drives grid strain and price rises.
Higher wholesale power costs feed electricity inflation.

E&E (1 Jul) confirms 50-60 GW decade deficit and a one-time backstop auction. Evidence is 4-5 months old. 'Is running a one-time backstop procurement' is stale: the auction window (30 Sep-21 Oct) has passed, so say it was proposed, outcome not checked. SPARC '75% built' is a June figure and may be out of date. Story 3 date '2026-08' is inferred; story 4 (May) not fetched.

desks.name: War & Geopolitics
desks.midnight_definition: Direct, sustained armed conflict between major powers (for example US-China, US-Russia or NATO-Russia), with the potential for nuclear escalation.
desks.headline: Xi, Trump, Putin meet in Shenzhen today; Gulf attacks and Hormuz closure persist
desks.summary: The first-ever China-Russia-US leaders' meeting is due in Shenzhen on 19 November on APEC's sidelines, with arms control and Iran expected on the US agenda and no outcome yet. In the Gulf, Iran kept attacking ships and fired drones at a US radar at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa base (intercepted) on 17 November while Qatar convened new talks and Trump said the US blockade stays. In Ukraine, Kyiv struck the Kerch Strait Bridge and Russian refineries, Russia kept hitting the grid, and European regulators warned of nuclear-accident risk this winter.

top_stories.title: Qatar warns of 'grave danger' in Gulf, convenes new Iran talks; drones fired at US base in Bahrain
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Guards said they launched drones at a US radar in Bahrain (intercepted, no damage per Bahrain and CENTCOM); a tanker was hit again off Oman and Trump says the naval blockade continues. Direct US-Iran fire is spreading to Gulf host states.

top_stories.title: Xi, Trump and Putin set for first three-way talks in Shenzhen on 19 November
top_stories.why_it_matters: China confirmed the meeting; US officials expect to raise nuclear arms cuts and Iran but not Ukraine. Beijing says the US and Russia should cut their larger arsenals before it discusses its own, and Xi reportedly objected to Ukraine being included without Europe.

top_stories.title: ISW: Kerch Bridge struck, refineries hit, Russian drone raids on Ukraine's grid continue
top_stories.why_it_matters: Ukraine's drones disrupted the Kerch Bridge (partly reopened 16 Nov); Russia launched 158 Shahed-type drones overnight, cutting power in six regions. Starshield speed limits on Ukrainian drones entered a seventh day, per Ukraine's envoy.
top_stories.source_name: Institute for the Study of War / Critical Threats

top_stories.title: Iran denies talks with US, says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met
top_stories.why_it_matters: Tehran and Washington give opposite accounts of whether talks exist; maritime monitors counted at least 37 attacks on ships in October, the highest month of the war.

top_stories.title: Xi, Trump, Putin: what to expect at APEC trilateral
top_stories.why_it_matters: Sets the baseline: New START lapsed in February with no successor and the meeting is the first chance for a framework.

trajectory.six_months: Renewed large-scale US-Iran combat remains a live risk unless a phased Hormuz-for-blockade deal lands; Ukraine stays high intensity with strikes on energy and nuclear-plant safety worries through winter.
trajectory.two_years: With no New START successor and several active theaters, miscalculation risk among nuclear powers stays elevated; outcomes range from frozen conflicts to a Taiwan or NATO-flank crisis.

signals_to_watch: Readouts and any joint statement from the 19 November Shenzhen trilateral
Outcome of the Qatar-hosted US-Iran contacts and any Hormuz reopening or blockade change
Further Iranian strikes on US assets in Gulf states or on shipping
Ukraine winter energy strikes and nuclear-plant safety warnings
US-China trade truce expiry on 10 January 2027

desks.name: Governance & Information
desks.midnight_definition: A breakdown of the shared ability to govern and to agree on facts, such that large societies can no longer correct their own mistakes.
desks.headline: Israel's Knesset flips speaker 66-52; Eisenkot still short of 61 as deadline nears
desks.summary: Rule-of-law indices (WJP, V-Dem, Freedom House, RSF) keep pointing down while the EIU shows a small uptick. In Israel the Knesset replaced Netanyahu's ally as speaker on 17 Nov by 66 to 52, giving Eisenkot's bloc control of the agenda, but no bloc has 61 seats and the mandate deadline is 6 December. Brazil's abuse-of-power litigation and the UN 2027 budget remain unresolved in sources reached this run.

top_stories.title: Knesset elects Eisenkot ally as speaker, 66 to 52, replacing Likud's Ohana
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows Eisenkot's bloc plus allies can win floor votes and now sets which bills advance, including a judicial committee and an inquiry into 7 October. Likud condemned the vote; Netanyahu remains caretaker until a government forms.

top_stories.title: Israel: Likud and Eisenkot's party open talks; rotation and Ben-Gvir are sticking points
top_stories.why_it_matters: Eisenkot rules out a rotation deal and talks with Otzma Yehudit; Liberman's party rejects a Likud-led government. Failure means new elections next year.

top_stories.title: Herzog tasks Eisenkot; recommendations 67 vs 46 for Netanyahu
top_stories.why_it_matters: Recommendation counts (67) differ from Eisenkot's own count of 74 lawmakers lacking confidence in Netanyahu, so the arithmetic is unsettled.

top_stories.title: WJP Rule of Law Index 2026: scores fall in 62% of countries, ninth year
top_stories.why_it_matters: A fourth, independent measure of institutional strength agrees with V-Dem and Freedom House on the direction of travel, though it measures legal-system performance rather than a loss of self-correction.

top_stories.title: Brazil: electoral court confirms Lula win; Flavio Bolsonaro drops annulment bid
top_stories.why_it_matters: The court said extended voting hours did not change the tally and rejected a claim about party observers. Bolsonaro dropped the annulment request and said he would instead pursue a case alleging abuse of power against the winning ticket. The source is affiliated with the winner's party, so framing may differ elsewhere.

top_stories.title: Israel: Eisenkot has until 6 Dec to form a government; blocs short of 61
top_stories.why_it_matters: After the 27 October election the seat split is 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, 53 for Netanyahu's bloc and 19 for two Palestinian-led factions. Disputes over rotation of the premiership and conscription exemptions are the main obstacles, and repeat elections remain possible.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an Israeli government or a path to new elections by late December, rulings on Brazil's abuse-of-power case, and the 2027 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions (March to May) showing whether erosion continues.
trajectory.two_years: The 2028 US cycle, AI-generated content at scale and UN funding limits are the main stressors; the question is whether courts and election bodies keep absorbing disputed outcomes.

desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: Iran bars enriched uranium leaving country; IAEA board outcome still unreported
desks.summary: No treaty has capped US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Bulletin's Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA board already found Iran in noncompliance and referred it to the UN Security Council on 9 September (23-3), where Russian and Chinese vetoes make action unlikely; inspectors have not located Iran's roughly 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium, and Iranian clerics are debating dropping the no-bomb pledge. North Korea is expanding enrichment and Russia-NATO nuclear signalling continues at a steady level.

top_stories.title: Iran security chief: no enriched material will leave the country
top_stories.why_it_matters: Rezaei also warned of consequences for new US strikes, hardening Tehran's position as the IAEA board meets and shutting off a stockpile-removal deal.

top_stories.title: Iran calls IAEA board resolutions flawed, rules out normal inspections
top_stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Vienna mission says normal safeguards cannot resume after attacks on its facilities and faults Grossi's reports; access deadlock persists.

top_stories.title: IAEA says Iran's highly enriched uranium still unaccounted for; board meets next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Inspectors have been shut out since the June 2025 strikes and cannot say where about 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is; Iran rules out regular monitoring for now.

top_stories.title: IAEA voices growing concern over Iran's underground enrichment plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: The confidential report says the agency lacks access to the Isfahan underground site and has lost continuity of knowledge over the stockpile.

top_stories.title: Iranian clerics push to drop the pledge against nuclear weapons
top_stories.why_it_matters: Carnegie's digest of a New York Times report says the idea has moved from the fringe to mainstream debate, a possible doctrinal shift.

top_stories.title: IAEA board votes 23-3 to report Iran to the UN Security Council
top_stories.why_it_matters: Second formal noncompliance step after June; Russia, China and Niger opposed, so Security Council sanctions look unlikely, while Iran ties access to a wider deal and talks remain stalled.

trajectory.six_months: Expect no binding US-Russia limits, an IAEA-Iran standoff with a stalled Security Council track, and further North Korean fissile-material growth. An explosive test by any state is possible but not the base case.
trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

Iranian statements or Majlis moves on NPT withdrawal or the no-weapons pledge

This is my own judgment, not a measurement.

desks.bottom_line: Treat the IAEA board outcome and any Iranian move on the no-bomb pledge as the next triggers; arms-control constraints remain absent.
desks.why_it_matters: Without caps or inspections, the US, Russia, China and the Middle East face higher miscalculation and proliferation risk, with Iran's unlocated stockpile the sharpest near-term gap.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: Egypt deepens fertiliser gas cuts to 33% as Hormuz stays severe and El Niño strengthens
desks.summary: UKMTO's weekly report (10 Nov) puts Hormuz transits about 65% below pre-conflict, with at least 11 ships attacked in the week to 6 Nov and JMIC holding its threat level at severe. Egypt's gas cut to fertiliser plants rose from 20% to 33% in early November with no end date, with urea near $535/t. NOAA's last primary page I could read shows a strengthening El Niño, and the FAO food price index (133.9 in October) remains mild, so hunger stress is concentrated in Sudan rather than global.

top_stories.title: UKMTO: Hormuz transits about 65% below pre-war, 11 ships hit in a week
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits; JMIC logged 177 incidents since 1 March and kept the threat at severe. Oil, LNG and fertiliser freight through the strait stay at risk, and counts are likely undercounted because ships switch off transponders.

top_stories.title: Egypt raises gas cuts to fertiliser plants to 33%, no end date
top_stories.why_it_matters: Mopco reported a 33% gas intake cut on 8 Nov, up from 20% a week earlier. Egypt has roughly 3.6 Mt of urea a year available for export, so prolonged cuts tighten supply ahead of 2027 planting; granular urea was about $535/t FOB, up roughly 17% on September.

top_stories.title: FAO food price index eases to 133.9 in October; sugar up for fourth month
top_stories.why_it_matters: The index is 5.9% above a year earlier and 16.4% under the March 2022 peak. Cereals fell 4.5% m/m (wheat, maize) while sugar rose 6.6% to its highest since December 2024, so the grain cushion is holding for now.

top_stories.title: IPC warns of famine risk in Darfur and Kordofan as El Niño drought bites
top_stories.why_it_matters: El Niño-linked drought affects over half of Sudan; poor crop growth covers 64% of cropland in North Darfur. About 19.5 million people faced acute food insecurity in May, 135,000 of them in Phase 5.

top_stories.title: NOAA CPC: El Niño advisory in force, strengthening, high odds of strong event into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: The CPC page I could fetch shows the 8 Oct issue: Niño-3.4 about +2.1C and over 83% odds of a strong or very strong event through Jan-Mar 2027, with a 54-83% chance of a record reading in overlapping seasons. A 12 Nov update exists but I could not read it directly.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser supply and cost will shape 2027 planting while El Niño impacts on Southern Hemisphere and Asian crops emerge; Sudan famine risk likely worsens without a large aid scale-up.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and a very strong El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises, the system probably absorbs it with rising regional hunger.

signals_to_watch: NOAA ENSO update 2026-12-10 and Australian, Indian, Brazilian crop estimates
FAO Food Price Index early December, especially vegetable oils and sugar
Weekly UKMTO/JMIC Hormuz transit and attack counts
Whether Egypt's 33% gas cut to Mopco and Kima extends or ends
Any new IPC famine classification in Sudan

Hormuz, an Egypt-led fertiliser squeeze and a strong El Niño are overlapping real drivers, but headline food prices are moderate, cereals are falling and no multi-region crop failure is yet visible. The Egypt cut deepening is a modest negative; I hold at 6.0 and someone could move it closer by weighting 2027 yield risk, or farther if Hormuz normalises.

desks.name: Robotics & Autonomy
desks.midnight_definition: General-purpose robots (humanoid or otherwise) doing ordinary physical work at scale more cheaply than human labour, across many job types rather than in a few controlled niches.
desks.headline: Autonomy spreads city by city; Tesla scale deferred, humanoids still unproven
desks.summary: Narrow autonomy keeps scaling: Baidu's Apollo Go reached 30 cities by October and Tesla opened unsupervised robotaxis in San Antonio on 9 Nov, but independent trackers showed only tens of unsupervised Tesla cars in April and Musk deferred large scale to a software overhaul due late 2026 to early 2027. Tesla's Q3 update floated 20,000 Optimus robots a week by 2027 while admitting the robot struggles with varied tasks, so humanoid claims remain far ahead of delivered work.

desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: HIV funding down 18% and US measles at a 35-year high as aid cuts bite
desks.summary: Health financing keeps shrinking: international HIV funding fell about 18% in 2025 to its lowest in nearly two decades (UNAIDS), the Global Fund closed its eighth replenishment at $12.64 billion, and total aid fell a record 23%. US measles reached 5,182 confirmed cases in 2026, the most since 1991, with a dispute over how deaths are counted. Demography keeps drifting down in Japan (record-low births) while South Korea's births rebound.

top_stories.title: UNAIDS: international HIV funding fell 18% in 2025, resurgence risk
top_stories.why_it_matters: Donor HIV money dropped from $8.8B to $7.3B; about 1.2 million new infections and 570,000 AIDS deaths in 2025, with infections rising in 21 countries. Without faster action UNAIDS projects over 3 million extra infections by 2030.

top_stories.title: US measles cases pass 5,000, highest in 35 years
top_stories.why_it_matters: CDC counts 5,182 cases and four deaths in 2026, over double 2025; Pennsylvania reports six deaths, and the CDC removed two from its tally after HHS questioned causation. Signals weakening vaccination coverage even in a rich country.

top_stories.title: Zero-dose children fall to 13.5 million in 2025, still above 2019
top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO/UNICEF estimates show a slight improvement over 2024 but 74 countries are worse than in 2019. Measles coverage has not recovered, with 1.8 million more unprotected children than in 2019.

top_stories.title: Japan births hit record low for tenth year, natural decline near 900,000
top_stories.why_it_matters: Preliminary 2025 births about 705,809 against roughly 1.61 million deaths, the largest natural population fall on record; pressure on pensions and care workforce keeps building.

top_stories.title: France adopts 2026 budget; pension reform suspension tied to it
top_stories.why_it_matters: After no-confidence motions failed, the budget was adopted; the Socialists won a suspension of the rise in retirement age until after the 2027 election. The Assembly had passed the social security bill narrowly in December 2025.

top_stories.title: South Korea births up 13% in August, 26th straight monthly rise
top_stories.why_it_matters: About 23,700 births in August; January-August up 14.5%. Still far below replacement, but decline is not uniform.

trajectory.six_months: Expect more US measles cases and first hard data on HIV, TB and malaria programme disruption as Global Fund 2026-2028 allocations take effect; East Asian birth data for early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: Further donor retrenchment would likely reverse immunisation and HIV gains in fragile settings, while ageing keeps forcing pension fights in Europe and Asia.

Funding cuts and US measles are real and worsening in places, but 2025 immunisation numbers improved slightly and Korea's births are rising, so evidence does not justify a move. Someone expecting faster health-system damage from aid cuts would set it lower.

desks.bottom_line: Treat health-funding retrenchment and falling vaccination as the live risk, and watch HIV and measles counts for measurable damage.
desks.why_it_matters: Low-income countries reliant on donor money for HIV, TB and vaccines are most exposed, as are children in under-vaccinated communities and ageing economies facing pension fights.

desks.name: Space
desks.midnight_definition: Permanent human presence beyond Earth becomes self-sustaining in practice: routine, cheap, fully reusable heavy lift plus a crewed base that persists.
desks.headline: First Starship ship catch done; booster lost, Flight 16 undated, FAA silent
desks.summary: Starship Flight 15 (13 Nov) put 26 Starlink V3 satellites up and the ship was caught by the tower on 14 Nov, a first, but the booster aborted after an early-ending boostback burn and was lost in the Gulf. SpaceX has set no Flight 16 date and the FAA had made no public statement on the booster loss as of 18 Nov. China's Mengzhou 1 orbital debut is still listed as planned for late 2026, and Haven-1 is no earlier than Q1 2027.

top_stories.title: Flight 16 undated; FAA licence, booster cause and cadence
top_stories.why_it_matters: Gives the clearest status of what follows Flight 15: licence revision 10 covered only Flight 15, so Flight 16 likely needs a licence change, and recent flight gaps of 46 to 66 days imply late December to mid-January at the earliest.

top_stories.title: SpaceX caught a Starship; what must be solved next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Rapid reuse needs both stages caught on one mission; the booster cause is open, and SpaceX says it aims to refly an upper stage by early next year.

top_stories.title: Starship Flight 15: ship reaches orbit, booster catch aborted
top_stories.why_it_matters: A ship catch is a step toward reuse, but the booster missed its tower catch, so rapid double reuse is still unproven.

top_stories.title: Mengzhou 1 still listed as planned for late 2026
top_stories.why_it_matters: China's crew capsule and Long March 10A orbital debut has no exact date and no launch evidence found; it gates China's 2030 crewed landing goal.

top_stories.title: Vast Haven-1 private station slips to no earlier than Q1 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: The first commercial station, a stepping stone to a post-ISS presence, is later than planned.

top_stories.title: China's Long March 10A booster flew a Mengzhou abort test
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows China rehearsing a reusable lunar-class booster and crew escape ahead of its 2030 landing goal.

trajectory.six_months: Expect a booster root-cause finding, a Flight 16 around late December to early 2027 at the earliest, a possible FAA decision on 100 launches a year, and a Mengzhou 1 attempt.
trajectory.two_years: Artemis III orbital rehearsal in 2027 and a landing attempt around Artemis IV in 2028 are the milestones; a persistent crewed base is still beyond this window.

desks.clock_reasoning: A ship catch is real progress but both-stage reuse, refuelling and a persistent base remain undemonstrated, and the booster loss shows reliability is unfinished. Landings are targeted for 2028 (US) and 2030 (China), so the threshold is about a decade out. This is judgment; someone expecting 2027 refuelling and weekly launches could say 8 minutes, someone weighting schedule slips could say farther.

desks.bottom_line: Treat Starship's first ship catch as progress, but plan on no Flight 16 or refuelling demo before roughly January 2027.
desks.why_it_matters: Reusable heavy lift sets the cost of lunar landings and large constellations; US and Chinese programmes, NASA and satellite operators are affected.
desks.confidence_basis: Two dated secondary sources agree on the Flight 15 facts, but no primary FAA or SpaceX page was read and several threads are unresolved.

desks.name: Natural Hazards & Wildcards
desks.midnight_definition: A natural or out-of-the-blue event (supervolcanic eruption, impactor, extreme solar storm, mega-quake) with global consequences that nobody was positioned for.
desks.headline: Quiet-to-minor solar storms and Kilauea cycle: hazards stay regional, clock holds
desks.summary: Hazard activity is elevated but regional. NOAA/USAF's 16 Nov report shows low solar activity (X-flare chance 5% a day on 17-18 Nov) with at most minor geomagnetic storms expected at mid-latitudes through 18 Nov; storm odds are higher at high latitudes. Kilauea's episode 56 fountained about 660 ft on 5 Nov and USGS gives a window of 18-22 Nov for episode 57. No new global-scale indicator was found; Campi Flegrei's strongest quake of the unrest (M4.7, 31 Jul) remains the main local-damage reference.

top_stories.title: Kilauea episode 56 fountains reach about 660 ft on 5 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: Part of a long-running episodic eruption in Hawaii; hazards are local (ash, gas, tephra) and the cycle is predictable.

top_stories.title: Kilauea recharging: glowing vents and rising tilt point to another fountain within days
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reporting based on USGS says the summit is reinflating ahead of episode 57, consistent with the 16-21 Nov forecast window.

top_stories.title: Solar activity report: low flare odds, minor storm possible 17-18 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: The official NOAA/USAF forecast shows low X-flare odds and only minor storming, so no grid or satellite threat at an extreme level.

top_stories.title: Banda Sea quake off Tual, Indonesia, rated M6.6 by USGS (carried)
top_stories.why_it_matters: Large intermediate-depth quake, USGS Green alert; magnitude reports conflict and no damage was confirmed in what I saw.

top_stories.title: Campi Flegrei M4.7 quake injures people and damages buildings near Naples (carried)
top_stories.why_it_matters: Strongest shock of the current unrest; shows real local damage potential near a densely populated caldera.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued Campi Flegrei quakes with a real chance of further M4+ events, routine global M6-7 quakes, repeating Kilauea episodes, and recurring G1-G2 storms as the solar cycle declines.
trajectory.two_years: Solar flare intensity should fall but extreme storms stay possible; Campi Flegrei unrest could plateau or escalate; Iceland's Reykjanes system is likely to erupt again with regional effect.

desks.clock_reasoning: Global-scale natural catastrophes are rare and none of the indicators checked is at alarm level, so the clock holds in the live-but-slow range. Campi Flegrei's yellow level since 2012 and 144 cm cumulative uplift by April 2025 mean a long-running local risk, not a global one. Someone could argue lower for grid and satellite fragility or higher on long base rates; coverage this run was thin.

desks.bottom_line: No action needed beyond routine monitoring; the live items are regional (Banda Sea aftershocks, Campi Flegrei, minor solar storms).
desks.why_it_matters: Regional quakes and volcanoes can hurt local populations and infrastructure; only a rare extreme solar storm or supervolcano would be global, and no sign of either appeared.
